n: Another message, now aimed at Tyre’s ruler.

f.w: The word of the LORD came again unto me
f.g: Chapter 28 targets Tyre’s king, then Sidon.

n: The prince of Tyre’s pride has swollen until he says, “I am a god, sitting on a divine throne in the heart of the seas.” But he is only a man, however godlike he imagines himself.

f.w: I am a God
yet thou art a man, and not God

n: With irony God says: you think you’re wiser than Daniel, that no secret is hidden from you.

f.w: wiser than Daniel
f.g: Daniel was known for God-given wisdom in Babylon; some think an ancient sage named Danel is meant.

n: His business skill brought him gold and silver.

f.w: thou hast gotten thee riches

n: His trading made him rich, and riches made him proud—a pattern the Book of Mormon calls the “pride cycle.”

f.w: thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches

n: Because he thinks of himself as divine…

f.w: set thine heart as the heart of God

n: …God will bring the most ruthless of nations against him to pierce his wisdom and defile his splendor.

f.w: the terrible of the nations

n: He will be thrown down to the pit and die a violent death at sea.

f.w: the pit

n: Will he still claim to be a god in front of his killer? In that moment he will be shown to be merely mortal.

f.w: I am God

n: He will die the shameful death of the uncircumcised—an Israelite way of saying a dishonorable, outcast death—at the hands of foreigners.

f.w: the deaths of the uncircumcised
f.g: An idiom for dying in disgrace (Phoenicians themselves practiced circumcision).

n: A new message: a lament for Tyre’s king.

f.w: Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me
f.g: Verses 11–19 move into language that seems larger than any human king.

n: The king was the very model of perfection—full of wisdom and perfect in beauty. Many readers, Christian and Latter-day Saint alike, see in this lament a picture of the fall of Lucifer, who also began in glory.

f.w: Thou sealest up the sum
f.g: You were the seal of perfection—the finished model.

f.w: take up a lamentation upon the king of Tyrus

n: He was in Eden, God’s garden, adorned with precious stones—several of which match the stones on the high priest’s breastplate. Music was part of his creation.

f.w: Eden the garden of God
every precious stone was thy covering
tabrets
f.g: Tambourines or settings for jewels; the Hebrew is uncertain.

n: He was an anointed guardian cherub on God’s holy mountain, walking among fiery stones—imagery of the heavenly court.

f.w: the anointed cherub that covereth
f.g: A guardian cherub, like those that covered the ark.

f.w: the holy mountain of God

n: He was blameless from the day of his creation until wickedness was found in him. Evil is not part of God’s creation; it enters by choice.

f.w: till iniquity was found in thee

n: His vast trade filled him with violence, so God cast him out from the mountain of God as unholy.

f.w: I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God

n: Pride in his beauty corrupted his wisdom. He will be thrown to the earth as a spectacle before kings.

f.w: Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty
I will cast thee to the ground

n: Dishonest trade profaned his sanctuaries, so a fire from within him will consume him to ashes before all. Sin carries the seeds of its own destruction.

f.w: I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee

n: All who knew him will be appalled; he will come to a dreadful end and be no more.

f.w: never shalt thou be any more

n: A new message about Sidon, Tyre’s older sister city.

f.w: Again the word of the LORD came unto me
f.g: A short oracle against Sidon follows.

n: Ezekiel turns his face against Sidon, about 25 miles north of Tyre.

f.w: Zidon
f.g: Sidon, a Phoenician city that gave its name to Phoenicians generally; home of Jezebel.

n: God will show his glory and holiness through judgment on Sidon.

f.w: I will be glorified in the midst of thee

n: Plague and the sword will fill her streets.

f.w: pestilence

n: Israel will no longer be pricked by hostile neighbors like briers and thorns.

f.w: a pricking brier

n: Looking forward: when God gathers Israel from the nations, he will show his holiness through them, and they will live in the land promised to Jacob.

f.w: When I shall have gathered the house of Israel

n: They will live securely, build houses, and plant vineyards—pictures of peace and permanence—after God judges their hostile neighbors.

f.w: build houses, and plant vineyards
